name: Plans and contracts
takeaways: The contract is the source of truth
Phases split time; line items hold products
Amendments apply from an effective date

learn.intro: A contract is the source of truth for a customer billing relationship. Once it is live, Zenskar runs two workflows from it at the same time: billing (invoices, payments) and revenue recognition.

cards.title: Contract
cards.body: Holds the customer, business entity, currency, start date and line items.
cards.example: Acme Inc, USD, starting Jan 15, with two products.

cards.title: Line item
cards.body: Each product added to a contract. Either point-in-time or period-of-time.
cards.example: A seat license (period) and API calls (point).

cards.title: Phase
cards.body: A time-based segment with its own dates and terms. Types: active, trial, pause.
cards.example: A 30-day trial, then a Standard phase. Invoicing starts after the trial.

cards.title: Plan
cards.body: A reusable pattern of products and features. Contracts built from it inherit them.
cards.example: A "Growth" plan used as the base for 20 customer contracts.

cards.title: Amendment
cards.body: A change applied from an effective date. Zenskar reshapes affected invoices without manual credit notes.
cards.example: A price change effective Jun 1 only affects invoices from Jun 1.

cards.title: Status
cards.body: A contract is drafted first and billing starts once it is active. It ends as expired.
cards.example: Stay in draft while terms are reviewed, then activate.

edgeCases: Customer is fixed. The customer on a contract cannot be changed after creation.
End date. The newer contract model currently requires an end date, so open-ended contracts are not supported yet. Older docs describe it as optional.
Concurrent edits. If two people save at once, the second save is rejected with a conflict error.
Line-item level only. In the newer model, discounts and minimum commitments work per line item, not at contract level.
No change log. A readable amendment history does not exist yet beyond the contract version number.
Retroactive changes. Only one rule for how retroactive billing changes affect invoices can be active on a contract.
At least one phase. A contract needs a phase before it can be activated, and phases must sit inside the contract dates.

groups.title: Operations in the reference
items: Contracts: list, create, get by ID, update, delete (must not be active)
Create contract phase and phase pricing
Pause, update pause, resume, expire contract
Plans: list, create, get, update, delete; phases and phase pricing; create new version

quiz.question: What is the source of truth for a customer billing relationship in Zenskar?
quiz.explanation: The contract holds the customer, currency, dates and line items that drive billing and revenue recognition.

quiz.question: You need to move a contract to a different customer. What happens?
options: The customer cannot be changed after creation
quiz.explanation: The customer on a contract cannot be changed after the contract is created.

quiz.question: Two teammates save the same contract at the same time. What happens?
options: The second save is rejected with a conflict error
quiz.explanation: This prevents one save from silently overwriting the other.

quiz.question: A contract is created from a plan. What does it inherit?
options: All products and features of the plan
quiz.explanation: A plan is a reusable pattern; a contract based on it inherits its products and features.

quiz.question: What does an amendment with an effective date do?
options: Applies from that date forward and reshapes affected invoices
quiz.explanation: Zenskar reshapes the affected invoices without manual credit notes or reconciliation.

qa.question: Contract vs plan?
qa.answer: A plan is a reusable template. A contract is customer-specific and drives billing. A contract created from a plan inherits its products and features.

qa.question: Phase vs line item?
qa.answer: A phase is a time segment with its own dates and terms. A line item is a product on the contract.

qa.question: Draft vs active contract?
qa.answer: Draft has not started billing and can be edited or deleted freely. Active is live and generating invoices.

qa.question: Pause vs expire?
qa.answer: Pause suspends a contract and can be resumed. Expire ends it; expired is final.

qa.question: Trial vs active phase?
qa.answer: A trial phase delays invoicing until it ends. An active phase bills normally.

qa.question: Amendment vs new contract?
qa.answer: An amendment changes the existing contract from an effective date and reshapes affected invoices. A new contract is a separate agreement.

qa.question: Contract-level vs line-item-level discounts?
qa.answer: In the newer model discounts and minimum commitments work per line item only. Contract-level discounts are listed as not yet available.

qa.question: Contract start date vs anchor date?
qa.answer: Start date is when billing begins. Anchor date aligns billing cycles regardless of start.

qa.question: 30-day trial then paid?
qa.answer: A trial phase followed by an active phase on the same contract.

qa.question: Ramp pricing in year one?
qa.answer: Use phases: one per stage with its own pricing.

qa.question: Seasonal customer wants to pause?
qa.answer: Pause with a start date and optionally a resume date.

qa.question: Customer upgrades mid-year?
qa.answer: Amend the contract with an effective date for the new terms.

qa.question: Standard offerings for many customers?
qa.answer: Create a plan and base contracts on it.

qa.question: A subsidiary uses the service but another entity pays?
qa.answer: Set the invoice payer customer on the contract, or bill the parent customer.

qa.question: Bill all contracts on the same day?
qa.answer: Set the same anchor date, or use last day of month.

qa.question: Can I change a contract's customer?
qa.answer: No. It cannot be changed after creation.

qa.question: Does a contract need an end date?
qa.answer: The newer model requires one; older docs describe it as optional.

qa.question: Two people edit at once?
qa.answer: The second save is rejected with a conflict error; reload and reapply.

qa.question: Can I delete an active contract?
qa.answer: Only draft contracts can be deleted. Expire an active one.

qa.question: Can phases overlap or fall outside the contract?
qa.answer: No. Phases must not overlap and must sit within contract dates.

qa.question: Which status changes are allowed?
qa.answer: Draft to active, active to expired, paused to active or expired. Expired and disputed are final.

qa.question: What time does expiry happen?
qa.answer: End of the given day (23:59:59.999999). The date defaults to today.

qa.question: What can I set as status when creating a contract?
qa.answer: Only draft or active. Pausing and expiring use their own actions.

qa.question: Can AI create a contract?
qa.answer: The docs describe a flow that extracts contract terms from a raw document.

qa.question: Which renewal policies exist?
qa.answer: The API lists renew_with_default_contract, renew_with_existing and do_not_renew, but currently only do_not_renew is supported.
